clue.text: Carefree young lady broadcasting

blocks.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering society
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A young woman without a care in the world presenting a radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes someone suave and lighthearted, with a relaxed confident manner free of worry.

clue.text: Part of 10: some little wader coming up

indicators.note: some of a phrase means only a portion of its run of letters is used
in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of little and the start of wader, read upwards

explanation.surface: A small wading bird rises from the water, part of some scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is BOOT, and a welt is the strip of leather joining a boot's upper to its sole.
explanation.definitionFit: A welt is the leather strip stitched between the upper and sole of a shoe or boot, so it is one component.

clue.text: Call sailor to seize control

blocks.note: a greeting called out
Jack, from Jack Tar, is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for a seaman to take over the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to take over a vehicle or plane by force, commandeering it from its crew.

clue.text: Notice change

blocks.note: to spot something is to notice it
change is coins, ready money

explanation.surface: Pay attention to some alteration, or spot the coins you have been given.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also hints at money you can see and pay over at once, which is what spot cash is.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot cash is money paid immediately on delivery, coins and notes handed over on the spot.

clue.text: Cover freedom of movement in film script

blocks.note: a screen covers or shields something
play is slack, room to move, as in a loose rope

explanation.surface: A stunt performer's harness must be covered yet allow movement in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay is the written text of a movie, with its dialogue and directions for the actors.

clue.text: Cape in South America

blocks.note: surface reading: a headland on the South American coast, like Cape Horn
setter's reading: a cape is a sleeveless cloak, and this one is the traditional South American kind

explanation.walkthrough: Cape looks geographical; it is a garment, a blanket with a hole for the head worn in the Andes.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a sleeveless cloak worn over the shoulders, originating among the peoples of South America.

clue.text: Vegetable Eric and Alec cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated soil is turned over and worked, so the letters are dug up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two allotment gardeners, Eric and Alec, grew a root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeriac is a variety of celery grown for its swollen edible root, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Word game: first clue's a brute!

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter only of the following word

blocks.note: the opening letter of clue
Rambo, the Stallone action hero, stands for a violent brute

explanation.surface: A frustrated solver declares that the first clue of a word game is a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Crambo is an old parlour game in which players find rhymes for a given word.

clue.text: Single out for breaking ground in advance

blocks.note: a pick is the tool used to break up hard ground
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: Someone is chosen to start digging ahead of the others.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick on someone is to choose them for criticism or bullying, selecting them from a group.

clue.text: Part of car for sale?

definitions.note: the word that precedes 'sale' in the name of a market, not a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: the luggage compartment at the back of a British car, the American trunk
second meaning: the word that goes with 'sale' for a British market where people sell goods from parked cars

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose second half: a car-boot sale is a British flea market where sellers lay out goods from their car's luggage space.
explanation.definitionFit: The boot is the storage compartment at the back of a British car, and gives its name to car-boot sales.

clue.text: A time, a period in jail, if really necessary

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
a stretch is slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A prisoner is told a spell inside will be imposed only when unavoidable.
explanation.definitionFit: At a stretch means with difficulty or only by making an extra effort, used of something barely possible.

clue.text: Mother to question the material

blocks.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
to question is to ask

explanation.surface: Mum is about to ask what the fabric is.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a rich patterned fabric, originally silk woven in Damascus, used for tablecloths and curtains.

clue.text: Plant a tattered sun-hat after a break

indicators.note: something tattered is ragged and torn apart, so the letters are scattered into a new order
after sends the piece before it to follow the piece that comes next in the clue

blocks.note: taken as written
a gap is a break or interval
the letters of sun-hat in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener's worn-out sun hat is replaced after a tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: The tattered sun-hat comes after a break, so A and GAP lead; the first 'a' only belongs to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Agapanthus is a garden flower from southern Africa, known as the African lily, with blue flower heads.

clue.text: Mastermind drops book in fight

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
rain falls in drops
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A genius lets fall a book during a scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind is a British television quiz, which suits the clue; the pieces are joined with book first, then drops, then fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainbox is an informal word for a very clever person, someone who could plan anything.

clue.text: One's missing on a flower. Is that so?

indicators.note: missing means the item named just before is absent from what follows

blocks.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
taken as written
a lily is a flower
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a bloom has a petal missing and asks in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower here is a bloom, not the crossword river; removing one I from LILY leaves LLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Really? is an exclamation of surprise or doubt, asking whether something said is actually true.

clue.text: Disregard switching parts to make an inspection

indicators.note: switching parts means the word's two halves change places

blocks.note: to overlook something is to disregard it

explanation.surface: An inspector ignores protocol and swaps components when checking a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves of OVERLOOK trade places, turning neglect into its opposite, careful scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: To look over something is to examine or inspect it, usually quickly, checking for faults.

clue.text: Discussion about the French holiday place

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: a chat is an informal discussion
le is French for the

explanation.surface: People talk about the French resort where they will spend their vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden house of the Alpine kind, typically rented by skiers or holidaymakers.

clue.text: Phoney art spied, having made a tedious journey

indicators.note: something phoney is fake, not genuine, so these letters are not in their true order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A forger's work was spotted after the detective trudged a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly over a long distance, trudging along.

clue.text: An official position portrayed in "OT"

blocks.note: first meaning: a minor parish or college officer
second meaning: the job held by Mr Bumble in Oliver Twist

explanation.walkthrough: OT looks like the Old Testament, but here it abbreviates Dickens's Oliver Twist, in which pompous Mr Bumble holds this parish office.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle was a parish officer who kept order in church and administered poor relief, as Mr Bumble does.

clue.text: Sleepy old English mascot, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged some other way

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drowsy old team mascot, perhaps the English lion, nods off.
explanation.definitionFit: Comatose means in a deep unconscious state, and informally means extremely drowsy or lethargic.

clue.text: A player, 10, is changed

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters appear in a different order

blocks.note: the answer to 10-across
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer's tenth man is substituted.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist is a musician who plays the oboe, a performer in an orchestra or band.

clue.text: Acceptable time for 23s?

blocks.note: surface reading: a convenient moment
setter's reading: 23 is POSTHOLDER, and the most welcome time for anyone in a job is when wages arrive

explanation.walkthrough: The 23s are employees, and the day they receive their wages is the time most acceptable to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Payday is the regular day on which employees receive their salary or wages.

clue.text: To some extent is left in the political group

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a party is a political group
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A commentator says the party has moved leftwards somewhat.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly means in part, not wholly, describing something only to a limited degree.

clue.text: Sack, possibly, for one with the job

blocks.note: first meaning: a mail sack, read as something holding letters
second meaning: someone who holds an official post

explanation.walkthrough: Sack suggests dismissal, the opposite of having a job; here it is a bag that holds mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A postholder is a person occupying a particular post or office, an employee in that role.

clue.text: Manage officer's exercises

blocks.note: CO is a commanding officer
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: An officer runs the troops' training drills.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to deal effectively with something difficult, getting by successfully.

clue.text: A crop of trite material?

blocks.note: first meaning: cereal grain grown in fields
second meaning: sentimental, hackneyed stuff, as in corny jokes

explanation.surface: A harvest of stale, unoriginal stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is both a cereal grown in fields and an informal term for banal, sentimental writing or humour.

clue.text: Fly? A second half of instruction*s needed

indicators.note: half of means only one of the two equal parts of the next word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
tutelage is instruction or teaching

explanation.surface: An insect in the soup; a moment's guidance is required.
explanation.walkthrough: The asterisk stands in for an apostrophe: instruction's needed. Fly in British slang means sharp, knowing, not easily fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and quick to spot an advantage, matching the British informal adjective for streetwise.

clue.text: Seen in dark room: size of print by unusual glare. Right?

definitions.note: a description of the thing, not a synonym

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal pattern, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: an en is a printer's unit of width
the letters of glare in a new order
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A photographer in the darkroom worries that harsh light will spoil the print size.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlarger is the projector used in a photographic darkroom to make bigger prints from negatives.
